misconceptions.description: Opening a data write-up by describing the data-gathering process instead of stating the finding and its implication
misconceptions.trigger: learner leads with 'we collected data' rather than the headline result
misconceptions.feedback: Lead with the finding and what it means, then give the supporting numbers, source, and time range. Process belongs in the method note, not the headline.

misconceptions.description: Claiming one event caused another just because they happened in sequence, without ruling out other explanations
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes 'X went up after Y, so Y caused X'
misconceptions.feedback: Sequence is not proof of cause. Note the correlation and name what else (season, ad, holiday) could explain the change.

misconceptions.description: Using dramatic language like 'skyrocketed' for a small change, so the narration overstates what the data shows
misconceptions.trigger: learner keeps inflated wording that does not match the actual numbers
misconceptions.feedback: Match the words to the magnitude. State the actual percentage and reject AI or draft wording that exaggerates the size of the change.
